name: Larkspur estate
description: A fictional financial-services group's control posture as its systems export it each day (ADR 0020): the organisation and its leaders from HR, about 2,400 applications from the CMDB, the cloud inventory, 46 shared platforms, a catalogue of 14 controls mapped to the frameworks, the risk register, the findings ledger and twelve evidence feeds. The bronze notebook judges every feed as it arrives; the silver notebooks conform the organisation, the applications and the evidence, and tell the posture a person reads. A synthetic dataset: no real company or person is its subject.

sources.description: The HR system's daily extract of the organisation: every unit (the group, its segments, business units, departments and teams) with its parent, its leader, and anyone acting for a vacant or absent one
The leaders in the HR extract: each with their title, manager, unit and status (active, on leave, or left in the last thirty days)
The CMDB's applications: the owning team, tier, exposure, data class, datastore, hosting, site, runtime platform and lifecycle, with when each record last changed
The cloud inventory: resources counted by application tag in each account

The GRC tool's control catalogue: each control's CSF 2.0 function and category, weight and cadence, which applications it applies to, what it depends on, what compensates for it and the kind of platform that provides it
Each control mapped to framework requirements (NIST CSF 2.0, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, PCI DSS v4.0.1, SOC 2), with how the two relate
The risk register: every version of every exception, with its approver, reason, validity and status that day
The vulnerability scanners and penetration tests: open findings, those fixed in the last thirty days, and one scan-information row an application scanned, saying whether the scanner logged in

TLS on exposed endpoints: the ingress, the certificate's issuer, the protocol offered and the certificate's expiry. One row an application it applies to (live internet- and partner-facing applications)
The web application firewall in front of internet-facing applications: its ingress, its mode and its ruleset’s age. One row an application it applies to
Yearly penetration tests for exposed tier 1 and 2 applications: the last test, the next due date and the open high findings
Encryption at rest for applications with a datastore: the store and its key store
Yearly key rotation for regulated data: the key store, the last rotation, the next due date and the key's age
Backups for the applications we host that keep data: the controller, the last job's state, the last success and the recovery point
Yearly disaster-recovery exercises for tier 1 applications: the last exercise, the next due date and whether the recovery time was met
MFA for every live application: the identity provider, the share of users registered and whether MFA is enforced. Registered is not enforced
Quarterly access reviews for applications with confidential or regulated data: the last review, the next due date, the reviewers and the access revoked
Central logging for the applications we host: the pipeline, the forwarder's certificate issuer, the last event received and the retention
Privileged accounts of tier 1 and 2 applications: the vault, the accounts, and how many are not vaulted
Endpoint detection on the hosts of the applications we host: hosts, hosts reporting, hosts in reduced functionality and the sensor version
The architecture inventory: each shared platform, its kind and its site
What each platform depends on, and the controls it provides to the applications on it (common or hybrid)

description.purpose: The organisation, one row a unit, for every roll-up

description.usage: Join an application’s owner unit or a level’s unit by org_unit_id

columns.name: path
columns.description: Its path from the segment down

columns.description: Its own leader, acting, or inherited from above

description.purpose: The applications, one row each, with their owner chain

description.purpose: One row a finding with its SLA, for the vulnerability SLA report and the auditors
description.limitations: Open findings and those fixed in the last thirty days; a finding reported again keeps its first-found date
description.usage: Count overdue findings by severity or application

columns.name: source
columns.description: Found by the scanner or a penetration test

columns.name: overdue
columns.description: Whether it is past its SLA

description.limitations: A score is only as good as its coverage: read the two together

description.usage: Read a leader’s units by level; the score and coverage are tier-weighted
